case.objective: Investigate an unexplained long-term acceleration observed in deep-space spacecraft tracking.

observations.observation: Doppler tracking data from two distant spacecraft showed a small, persistent acceleration approximately directed toward the Sun.
The effect was small but persisted over a long period of tracking.
The two spacecraft had broadly similar spacecraft designs and both exhibited the unexpected acceleration.
The spacecraft generated electrical power using radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs).
The RTGs released substantial thermal energy into space.
The spacecraft had a large high-gain antenna and other surfaces capable of emitting or reflecting thermal radiation.
The observed acceleration was approximately constant over substantial portions of the tracking period.
Navigation models included gravitational forces and known spacecraft forces, but the observed motion initially showed a residual unexplained component.

constraints: Do not assume new physics unless conventional explanations are insufficient.
Consider spacecraft-systematic effects before proposing exotic explanations.
Every major hypothesis must identify supporting and contradicting evidence.

established_observations: Doppler tracking of two distant spacecraft revealed a small, persistent acceleration directed approximately toward the Sun (OBS-01).
The observed acceleration persisted over a long tracking duration (OBS-02).
The two spacecraft possessed broadly similar designs and both showed the unexplained acceleration (OBS-03).
Radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs) were used for electrical power generation on the spacecraft (OBS-04).
Substantial thermal energy was emitted into space by the RTGs (OBS-05).
The spacecraft featured a large high-gain antenna and additional surfaces that can emit or reflect thermal radiation (OBS-06).
The magnitude of the acceleration was approximately constant over major portions of the tracking timeline (OBS-07).
Standard navigation models incorporating gravity and identified spacecraft forces left a residual unexplained motion component (OBS-08).
important_clues: The presence of the anomaly across two distinct spacecraft with similar physical configurations suggests a systematic or design-related origin rather than an isolated instrument glitch (OBS-03).

The presence of high thermal energy output from RTGs alongside asymmetric reflection/emission surfaces (high-gain antenna) provides a potential physical mechanism for anisotropic radiation force (OBS-04, OBS-05, OBS-06).
The approximately constant nature of the force over long observation windows constrains temporal behavior for candidate forces (OBS-02, OBS-07).
The directional orientation of the acceleration is approximately aligned toward the Sun (OBS-01).
relationships: OBS-01 and OBS-03 connect trajectory tracking to spacecraft hardware design, showing that identical design characteristics correlate with identical anomalous acceleration vectors.
OBS-04, OBS-05, and OBS-06 link thermal energy generation (RTGs) directly to physical spacecraft geometry (high-gain antenna and surfaces) capable of interacting with radiation.
OBS-01, OBS-07, and OBS-08 link navigation model residuals to a specific vector (sunward) and temporal behavior (approximately constant over long durations).
uncertainties: Whether the net directional thermal radiation force emitted or reflected by the spacecraft geometry is sufficient in magnitude and direction to explain the residual acceleration.
Whether the acceleration remains strictly constant indefinitely or decays over longer time horizons.
Whether the residual component stems from onboard spacecraft systematic forces or an external force.
The exact directional alignment between the thermal radiation anisotropy axis and the sunward Doppler tracking vector.
discriminating_evidence: Quantitative thermal-recoil modeling and directional analysis of RTG heat radiation reflecting off the high-gain antenna and spacecraft surfaces.
Temporal tracking of the acceleration magnitude over extended timeframes to evaluate whether it decays synchronously with RTG thermal power output or remains constant.
Detailed telemetry data on onboard thermal distribution and directional radiation patterns across different operational modes.
Comparison with deep-space trajectory residuals from spacecraft possessing non-RTG power sources or significantly different structural geometries.

core_anomalies: Unexplained residual acceleration directed approximately toward the Sun observed in Doppler tracking after incorporating standard gravitational and identified non-gravitational models (OBS-01, OBS-08).
Identical unexplained trajectory residuals appearing across two distinct spacecraft sharing similar structural configurations (OBS-03).
unexpected_patterns: The anomalous acceleration maintains an approximately constant magnitude over long observation windows (OBS-02, OBS-07).
Consistent sunward directional orientation of the residual force vector across different trajectories and times (OBS-01).
possible_relationships_to_investigate: Correlation between shared physical spacecraft geometry (high-gain antenna, reflective surfaces) and the observed directional vector of the force (OBS-03, OBS-06).
Relationship between high thermal energy generation from onboard RTGs and potential anisotropic radiation emission or reflection off spacecraft structures (OBS-04, OBS-05, OBS-06).
Coupling between the temporal profile of the force and the thermal decay rate of onboard power systems (OBS-05, OBS-07).
contradictions_or_tensions: The observation of an approximately constant acceleration magnitude over extended timelines (OBS-07) stands in tension with the expected temporal decay of RTG thermal power generation (OBS-04, OBS-05).
Standard celestial mechanics and spacecraft force models predict zero motion residual, contradicting persistent Doppler tracking discrepancies (OBS-01, OBS-08).
questions_for_hypothesis_agent: Is the observed vector strictly aligned toward the Sun, toward Earth (line of sight), or along the spacecraft physical symmetry/spin axis?
Does anisotropic thermal recoil modeling produce sufficient force magnitude and correct directional alignment to explain the residual acceleration without exceeding thermal energy budgets?
Does temporal tracking over longer horizons reveal a subtle decay in acceleration magnitude proportional to RTG power decay, or is the force genuinely time-invariant?
Could an unmodeled external environmental force produce an identical sunward residual across independent spacecraft trajectories?

hypotheses.name: Anisotropic Spacecraft Thermal Radiation Recoil
hypotheses.explanation: The residual acceleration is caused by anisotropic thermal emission or reflection of heat generated by onboard Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators (RTGs) reflecting off spacecraft structural components (such as the high-gain antenna), imparting a net momentum flux along the spacecraft symmetry/spin axis.
supporting_evidence: Correlation between shared physical spacecraft geometry/reflective surfaces and the observed direction of the force vector (OBS-03, OBS-06).
Presence of high thermal energy generation from onboard RTGs capable of imparting recoil forces (OBS-04, OBS-05).
Appearance of identical unexplained residuals across two distinct spacecraft sharing similar structural configurations (OBS-03).
contradicting_evidence: The observed approximately constant acceleration magnitude over long observation windows (OBS-02, OBS-07) stands in tension with the expected temporal decay rate of RTG thermal power generation (OBS-04, OBS-05).
Current observational correlation between force direction and physical geometry does not by itself establish direct physical causation without quantitative thermal modeling.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Construct a high-fidelity finite-element thermal model of spacecraft geometry and compare calculated thermal recoil decay profiles against long-baseline Doppler residual time-series to check for subtle decay.

hypotheses.name: Systematic Tracking, Propagation, or Frame Modeling Artifact
hypotheses.explanation: The observed residual acceleration is an unmodeled systematic error in Doppler signal processing, radio propagation modeling, or line-of-sight coordinate transformations, resulting in an apparent trajectory deviation rather than a physical acceleration acting on spacecraft mass.
supporting_evidence: The anomaly is detected via residual analysis in Doppler tracking data (OBS-01, OBS-08).
The force vector maintains a consistent orientation approximately aligned toward the Sun/Earth line-of-sight (OBS-01).
contradicting_evidence: Standard gravitational and identified non-gravitational models have already been incorporated into trajectory analysis without resolving the Doppler discrepancies (OBS-01, OBS-08).
Identical residual profiles are observed independently across two distinct spacecraft trajectories (OBS-03), reducing the likelihood of a localized single-station receiver artifact.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Perform cross-validation of Doppler tracking data against independent positional measurements (such as range or optical tracking) and test for systematic variations correlated with Earth-Sun-spacecraft orbital geometry changes.

hypotheses.name: Unmodeled External Heliospheric Drag or Mass Distribution Force
hypotheses.explanation: The spacecraft are experiencing a persistent physical acceleration caused by an unmodeled external environmental interaction, such as drag from heliospheric dust/gas or gravitational influence from an unidentified solar system mass distribution.
supporting_evidence: The residual force exhibits a consistent sunward orientation across different trajectories and observation periods (OBS-01, OBS-03).
The acceleration magnitude remains approximately constant over extended observation windows (OBS-02, OBS-07), consistent with traversal through a roughly uniform background environment.
contradicting_evidence: Standard celestial mechanics models predict zero trajectory residual after accounting for known gravitational sources (OBS-01, OBS-08).

An environmental drag force typically scales with spacecraft cross-sectional area and relative velocity, which is difficult to reconcile with a constant sunward vector across varied trajectories without specific fine-tuning.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Compare residual acceleration profiles between spacecraft with substantially different area-to-mass ratios and velocities traversing similar heliospheric distances.

key_unknowns: Whether the residual vector is precisely aligned with the Sun, the Earth line-of-sight, or the spacecraft physical symmetry/spin axis.
Whether long-baseline tracking data contains a subtle, previously unresolved exponential decay in acceleration magnitude proportional to RTG power decay.
The exact fraction of total RTG thermal output that is radiated anisotropically by the spacecraft structural geometry.
Current evidence is insufficient to definitively separate structural/thermal causes from tracking systematic errors without quantitative thermal modeling and multi-angle trajectory analysis.
recommended_next_tests: Develop a full-geometry anisotropic thermal radiation model incorporating RTG thermal decay profiles and surface reflectivity characteristics.
Decompose tracking residuals into separate vectors (Sun-directed, Earth-directed, spin-axis-directed) over varying Earth-Sun-spacecraft geometry angles.
Perform extended time-series statistical analysis on Doppler residuals to bound or detect potential magnitude decay over long observation horizons.

main_weaknesses: Direct contradiction between the observed approximately constant acceleration magnitude over long observation windows (OBS-02, OBS-07) and the expected exponential temporal decay of RTG thermal power generation (OBS-04, OBS-05).

Observational correlation between geometry/RTG presence and force direction (OBS-03, OBS-06) confuses correlation with causation; without quantitative thermal momentum flux modeling, physical sufficiency remains unproven.
unsupported_assumptions: Assumes that thermal emission/reflection off spacecraft geometry produces sufficient net momentum flux to account for the observed acceleration magnitude.
Assumes the net thermal recoil vector maintains continuous alignment toward the Sun rather than strictly along the spacecraft physical spin/symmetry axis as orientation changes relative to the Sun.
evidence_that_would_falsify: Long-baseline Doppler residual time-series demonstrating complete time-invariance (zero decay) over observation horizons exceeding multiple RTG power decay half-lives.
Quantitative finite-element thermal radiation modeling proving that maximum available anisotropic thermal momentum flux is substantially smaller than the force required for the observed residual.
critiques.alternative_explanation: The residual force is an unmodeled systematic tracking artifact along the Earth-spacecraft line of sight (H2) or an external environmental interaction independent of internal power decay (H3).

main_weaknesses: Fails to explain why two distinct spacecraft sharing similar structural configurations exhibit identical residual acceleration profiles across independent trajectories (OBS-03).
Assumes unmodeled errors remain in Doppler processing or coordinate transformations despite standard gravitational and non-gravitational models already being incorporated (OBS-01, OBS-08).
unsupported_assumptions: Assumes a persistent systematic error exists in line-of-sight Doppler processing or frame transformations that mimics a constant, physical sunward acceleration force.
Assumes tracking artifacts manifest identically across different observation times, geometries, and independent spacecraft trajectories.
evidence_that_would_falsify: Cross-validation of trajectory residuals using independent non-Doppler positional measurements (e.g., direct range timing or optical tracking) that confirm physical trajectory displacement.
critiques.alternative_explanation: A real physical force acting on the spacecraft mass, such as internal anisotropic thermal recoil (H1).

main_weaknesses: Heliospheric drag forces scale with spacecraft cross-sectional area, relative velocity, and local density, contradicting the observation of a constant acceleration magnitude across varied trajectories (OBS-02, OBS-07).

Gravitational force from an unmodeled mass distribution would exhibit distance-scaling ($1/r^2$) and affect celestial bodies, contradicting a constant sunward vector (OBS-01, OBS-07) and existing gravitational model fits (OBS-08).
unsupported_assumptions: Assumes the existence of a uniform background heliospheric medium or mass distribution capable of exerting a constant sunward force without violating established celestial mechanics models.
Assumes environmental drag remains constant despite changing heliospheric distance and spacecraft velocity.
evidence_that_would_falsify: Demonstration that the residual acceleration magnitude is invariant to changes in spacecraft cross-sectional area, mass, or velocity.
Direct measurements showing local heliospheric density is orders of magnitude lower than required to produce observable drag forces.
critiques.alternative_explanation: Internal thermal radiation recoil (H1) or a systematic line-of-sight tracking artifact (H2).

cross_hypothesis_comparison.main_reason: Provides a physically grounded mechanism linked to shared spacecraft geometry (OBS-03, OBS-06), but suffers from severe tension with observed force constancy vs. expected RTG power decay (OBS-05, OBS-07).
Directly addresses the observation method (Doppler residual analysis OBS-01, OBS-08), but struggles to explain identical residual profiles across two independent spacecraft trajectories (OBS-03).
Requires unphysically fine-tuned environmental properties or mass distributions to explain a constant sunward vector without exhibiting expected velocity, area, or $1/r^2$ scaling.

critical_unknowns: The precise directional orientation of the force vector: whether strictly aligned toward the Sun, toward Earth (line-of-sight), or along the spacecraft physical spin/symmetry axis.
The presence or absence of a subtle exponential decay in residual magnitude over long time baselines matching RTG thermal decay.
The quantitative momentum flux budget available from anisotropic thermal radiation and reflection off spacecraft surfaces.
Current evidence is explicitly insufficient to uniquely distinguish between internal thermal recoil (H1), signal processing artifacts (H2), and external forces (H3).
recommended_discriminating_tests: Deconstruct Doppler tracking residuals into distinct geometric vector components (Sun-directed, Earth-line-of-sight, and spacecraft spin axis) across varying Earth-Sun-spacecraft orbital angles.
Construct a finite-element thermal model of spacecraft geometry to compute expected thermal momentum flux and compare predicted recoil decay curves against long-baseline temporal residual data.

Compare Doppler-derived residuals against independent non-Doppler tracking measurements (such as range timing) to test whether trajectory discrepancies represent physical acceleration or measurement artifacts.

Evaluate residual acceleration profiles across spacecraft with different cross-sectional areas and relative velocities to test for area/velocity scaling (falsifying environmental drag in H3 if invariant).

selection.reason: To quantitatively estimate the acceleration produced by anisotropic RTG thermal radiation and determine whether thermal recoil is physically sufficient to account for the residual acceleration.

inputs.note: The current blind case does not contain numerical thermal telemetry, so these values are demonstration parameters.
